**Key observations from test image:**
- Stem split longitudinally showing **white/cream pith** — clearly not brown
- Severely blackened, rotted root system — roots appear almost completely destroyed, dark/black
- No brown discoloration inside the stem pith

**Diagnosis reasoning:**
- White pith is the critical diagnostic feature: "The pith remains white, which distinguishes SDS from brown stem rot"
- The severely rotted, blackened roots match SDS root decay pattern
- The SDS reference image (bottom-left panel) shows an almost identical presentation — pulled plant with blackened root system and white internal stem tissue
- Brown Stem Rot is ruled out (would show brown pith)
- Phytophthora is ruled out (would show chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending upward from soil line)
